nodes.description: The bronchial epithelium, lung fibroblasts and endothelium exposed to the sensitizer release IL-8, IL-6 and IL-1beta, generate reactive oxygen species, lose MUC1, and upregulate endothelial adhesion molecules. This innate response licenses dendritic cell maturation but is not by itself specific to a sensitizer, which is why an irritant exposure can produce a similar picture without sensitization following.

nodes.description: Hapten-specific T cells expand and polarize toward a type 2 profile, with IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13 and airway eosinophilia. This establishes the immunological memory that gives sensitizer-induced occupational asthma its defining clinical features: a latency period before onset, and reproducible symptoms on re-exposure to that agent and not to others. Specific IgE may accompany it but frequently does not with low molecular weight agents.

nodes.description: In the irritant-induced stratum there is no haptenation and no agent-specific memory. A reactive inhaled irritant injures the epithelium directly, disrupting tight junctions and raising paracellular permeability, and the resulting inflammation produces asthma without a latency period. This is why irritant-induced occupational asthma begins within hours of a high-dose exposure rather than after months of low-level exposure.

The convergence point of both strata and the clinical disease. Airway smooth muscle contraction, airway hyperresponsiveness and variable airflow limitation, with the temporal pattern that defines the diagnosis: symptoms worse at work and improving away from it. Removal from exposure does not reliably resolve it, so this node represents a persistent state rather than a transient response to exposure. Both strata converge here by different routes: the sensitizer arm through hapten-specific memory, the irritant arm through direct epithelial injury. The `conforms_to` link is true of the sensitizer route; the irritant module's own consequence is mucociliary clearance failure rather than asthma, so it is deliberately not named as a second target.

nodes.description: A reactive low molecular weight chemical inhaled at the workplace binds nucleophilic residues on airway and serum proteins, generating the hapten-protein adduct that the immune system subsequently recognizes. This is the step that requires the agent to be chemically reactive, and it is why the low molecular weight agents behave differently from the protein allergens that sensitize directly.

nodes.description: Removing or substituting the sensitizer in the workplace so that workers are never exposed. This is a different intervention from the removal row above, which withdraws an already-affected worker: this one prevents the disease arising at all, and the evidence for it is the strongest in the field. Powder-free low-protein natural rubber latex gloves are the worked case, where substitution was followed by a sharp fall in new sensitization.
